Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the quick sync this morning. Per our conversation, I attached our most recent redlines to the standard Redwood DPA and the current subprocessor list. Key open items we flagged on our side:

- Confirmation that Redwood will include the EU SCCs (Module(s) 2/3) language plus a brief "bridge" clause to capture cross-border subprocessors where applicable.
- UK IDTA — we saw your note that Redwood prefers an addendum. Please confirm what the addendum will look like and whether the DPA can reference a separate execution flow.
- Subprocessors — we need an explicit attestation that any new subprocessor will be notified 30 days before onboarding.
- Audit scope — Bridgepoint generally looks for a 60-day notice and a remote-only audit; please confirm Redwood's acceptance.

Attachments: DPA_Bridgepoint_Redlines_v3.docx (redline), Subprocessor_List_20261112.csv

If the edits look good, legalops asked if we can route via DocuSign (we prefer Bridgepoint to sign first). I can generate the envelope and share a link once we get Redwood's final signoff on the two SCC/IDTA bullets above.

Appreciate the help — look forward to locking this so we can proceed with onboarding.

—Jordan

Jordan —

Thanks for the redlines and the subprocessor list. We've reviewed internally and the short version: we're comfortable moving forward with your edits after a couple of targeted clarifications. High-level responses below (I've attached an annotated DPA with inline comments).

1) SCCs / bridge language: Redwood accepts including the EU SCCs. We propose a short "compatibility" clause (see p.4 of the attached) which says: Redwood will apply the EU SCCs where required and will maintain a mapping of processing locations and subprocessors. This is primarily operational; legal is comfortable with the proposed wording provided it references the signed modules.

2) UK IDTA / addendum: We prefer a standalone UK addendum to avoid duplicative clauses in the main DPA. Our legal ops template for the IDTA addendum is in the drive link below — we can populate it and route alongside the DocuSign envelope.

3) Subprocessors: The current list looks fine. We can commit to 30 days' prior notice for new subprocessors as a contractual commitment; operationally we'll flag onboarding activities in the onboarding MRP. Please note we may have limited situations (emergency patching, disaster recovery) where notice is compressed — for that, we propose a carve-out with immediate notice-after-the-fact and a post-event summary.

4) Audit scope / notice: 60 days is reasonable for remote audits. Redwood cannot support on-site physical audits for security reasons, so remote-only with a stated scope (logs, config screenshots, SOC2 artifact reviews) is preferred.

Next steps I'm proposing:
- Karhtik (legal) to send final redlines on the bridge clause and the audit paragraph by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa (GTM/onboard) will prepare the DocuSign envelope and indicate sign order (Bridgepoint signs first).
- If Bridgepoint accepts the UK addendum flow, we'll attach that as a separate exhibit in DocuSign.

I've attached: DPA_Bridgepoint_Redlines_v3.docx (annotated), Subprocessor_List_20261112.csv. Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDPA-Bridgepoint

If that timeline works, Marissa will kick off the envelope once we have Karthik's note.

Best,

Priya Natarajan
Head of Customer Ops (Privacy & Compliance)
Redwood Inference

Team —

Quick legal redlines (annotated in the attached DPA):

- Bridge wording: tighten "mapping of processing locations" to explicitly reference subprocessors by legal entity + country. We should avoid an open-ended mapping; require Redwood to publish a console view and provide it upon request.

- SCCs modules: confirm we're inserting Modules 2 and 3 as appropriate, and include signature blocks for both the parties. If Bridgepoint requests Module 1/2/3 variants we need to be clear which modules are executed and where the data subjects are located.

- UK IDTA: agree with Priya — use an addendum template. Ensure the addendum references the DPA effective date and includes the UK-specific signature block.

- Audit carve-out: accept remote-only with 60 days' notice. Add sentence that Redwood will produce "operational evidence" within 20 business days of a request.

- Sign order: suggest we* sign second (Redwood signs after Bridgepoint) and set the DocuSign envelope to require sequential signing.

I'll upload a marked PDF with the changes. Marissa — please queue the DocuSign envelope with an instruction to attach the UK addendum as an exception exhibit (if Bridgepoint accepts that flow).

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
